text:
nina: FYI — AcmeHealth POC ran into a weird one. When they use streaming function calls + structured output behind their enterprise proxy, the client sees truncated JSON and then the model falls back to plain text. Customer is blocked for demo tomorrow.

jordan: ugh. any logs or a repro?

nina: they sent this snippet from the client logs: `JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at line 1 column 245` after ~3 chunks. They say it only happens when proxy inspection is on.

meera: which SDK and stream mode? SSE or websocket? and are they using function_call=auto or explicit?

nina: node sdk v0.9.2, streaming SSE (EventSource). function_call: "auto" and a response schema passed in as `response_schema` for structured output.

jordan: can you paste the request payload (sanitized)?

nina: here — they redacted PII but left structure: ```json
{
  "model":"open-redwood-3b",
  "stream":true,
  "function_call":"auto",
  "response_schema":{
    "type":"object",
    "properties":{
      "id":{"type":"string"},
      "result":{"type":"object"}
    },
    "required":["id","result"]
  }
}
```

ops-bot: note: TLS inspection proxies sometimes rewrite escape sequences and strip \n characters from SSE payloads (observed with certain vendor middleboxes).

sam: that matches — many enterprise DLP/IPS devices will sanitize control chars. If the SSE chunks lose the trailing `}` or a `\"` sequence gets altered, JSON decoding fails.

meera: plausible. Two quick workarounds: 1) switch to websocket streaming (less likely to be mutated by proxies), or 2) disable `response_schema`/structured enforcement on the stream and parse post-stream. Both preserve streaming latency but behave differently for downstream parsing.

jordan: what about function calls? if the model emits a function_call object across chunks and the proxy drops characters we risk partial JSON for the function args. Any safe fallback?

meera: we have a runtime option `structured_boundary=true` (internal flag) that emits a clear chunk delimiter and repeats a short checksum every N tokens so clients can detect truncation. Not enabled by default for hosted customers; needs eng opt-in for POC.

nina: customer asked about pricing impact if we enable a dedicated stream or the `structured_boundary` option — they want to know if costs jump for long streaming demos.

jordan: pinging pricing — @meera is there a perf/cost delta for boundary checks?

meera: overhead is small (~2-4% extra tokens due to checks). Main cost is runtime time for long-lived connections. For demos under 30m it's negligible on hosted, but for production with many concurrent streams recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) — predictable throughput + less noisy neighbors if proxies cause retransmits.

sam: security note: if we suggest websocket, confirm customer proxy allows websocket (some corp proxies block). Also need to get their proxy vendor details for our security questionnaire — some vendors have known TLS-inspection behavior.

jordan: next steps?

nina: proposed: 1) ask customer to try websocket stream for demo; 2) if websocket blocked, run a quick test with proxy off to reproduce; 3) meera to spin up a POC runtime with `structured_boundary=true` for testing; 4) sam to add vendor to questionnaire; 5) i'll send pricing note for 30/60/240 minute demo with hosted vs dedicated.

meera: I can have a debug runtime ready in ~2 hours. Will log streaming raw chunks for us to inspect.

sam: I'll draft a one-pager on proxy caveats and attach to your SSO/KMS questionnaire answers.

jordan: I'll prep a small client snippet for websocket usage and a fallback parser that tolerates truncated chunks (best-effort).

nina: thanks all — I'll update AcmeHealth and schedule the websocket test. If we can reproduce, we'll decide on enabling `structured_boundary` for their POC. :thumbsup:
